source: Zombicide 2nd Edition Rules & Missions, uploaded PDF

entries.title: Player Phase
entries.summary: Players activate their Survivors before the Zombies act.
details: The First Player takes their turn first; play then passes to the player on their left.
A Survivor initially has 3 Actions per Turn at Blue Danger Level, unless Skills grant additional Actions.
A player activates their Survivors one at a time and may choose their activation order.

entries.title: Zombie Phase
entries.summary: Resolve Zombie attacks and movement, then spawn new Zombies.
details: Each Zombie spends its Action on an Attack or a Move.
Resolve all Zombie Attacks before resolving Zombie Moves.
After activations, draw Zombie cards for active Spawn Zones, starting with the Starting Spawn Zone.

entries.title: End Phase
entries.summary: Clear Noise tokens and pass the First Player token.
details: Remove all Noise tokens from the board.
The First Player token passes to the player on the left.
Begin the next Game Round.

entries.title: Winning and losing
entries.summary: The team wins or loses together.
details: The team wins immediately when all Mission objectives are accomplished.
The team loses if a Survivor is eliminated, if the objectives can no longer be fulfilled, or if a Mission-specific losing condition is met.

entries.title: Zones
entries.summary: A Zone is a room indoors or an area bounded by street markings, walls and the board edge outdoors.
details: Inside a building, each room is a separate Zone.
Street Zones may extend across multiple tiles.
Actors move between Zones that share an edge; corners do not count, so diagonal movement is not allowed.

entries.title: Line of Sight
entries.summary: Line of Sight depends on whether the Actor is in a street or building Zone.
details: In street Zones, Line of Sight follows straight lines parallel to the board edges; it cannot go diagonally.
From a building Zone, an Actor sees through openings into connected Zones, but only 1 Zone away inside buildings.
From a street Zone into a building, Line of Sight reaches only 1 Zone into that building.
Closed doors block Line of Sight.

entries.title: Movement
entries.summary: Move between adjacent Zones without crossing walls or closed doors.
details: Street movement between empty Zones has no restriction.
Movement between a building and the street requires an open door or opening.
In buildings, Zones must be connected by an opening.
Entering a Zone containing Zombies ends the Move Action unless a Skill says otherwise.

entries.title: Survivor types
entries.summary: Classic Survivors usually start with 3 Health; Kids usually start with 2.
details: Kid Survivors can use Slippery once per Turn with a single Move Action.
A Survivor is eliminated when their Wound Bar reaches the bottom.

entries.title: Adrenaline and Danger Levels
entries.summary: Eliminating a Zombie normally grants 1 Adrenaline Point (AP).
details: Danger Levels are Blue, Yellow, Orange and Red.
Yellow is reached at 7 AP, Orange at 19 AP and Red at 43 AP.
Reaching a new Danger Level grants a Skill; Skills from earlier levels remain active.
The highest Danger Level reached by any Survivor determines which line of a Zombie Spawn card is used.

entries.title: Inventory
entries.summary: Each Survivor has 2 Hand slots and 3 Backpack slots.
details: Equipment in Hand slots can be used normally.
Equipment in Backpack slots cannot be used unless the card says it may be used in the Backpack.
A Survivor may discard cards at any time to make room.
A Reorganize/Trade Action lets a Survivor exchange any number of cards with one other Survivor in the same Zone, if both agree.

entries.title: Move
entries.summary: Move to an adjacent Zone, paying extra Actions to leave Zombies behind.
details: Spend 1 additional Action for each Zombie in the Zone being left.
Entering a Zone containing Zombies ends the Move Action unless a Skill allows otherwise.

entries.title: Search
entries.summary: Search an eligible building Zone for Equipment.
details: A Survivor may Search only a building Zone with no Zombies.
Draw the top Equipment card and either add it to the inventory, reorganizing for free, or discard it.
A Survivor can perform only one Search Action per Turn, even if the Action is free.

entries.title: Open a door
entries.summary: Use Equipment with the door-opening symbol; no roll is required.
details: Set or flip the Door token to its open side.
If the Equipment makes Noise when opening a door, place one Noise token in the Survivor's Zone.
Open doors cannot be closed again. Colored doors may require a Mission condition.

entries.title: Combat actions
entries.summary: Use a Melee or Ranged weapon equipped in a Hand slot.
details: Melee weapons attack Zombies in the Survivor's own Zone.
Ranged weapons target one Zone within the weapon's Range and Line of Sight, including Range 0 when permitted.
Survivors attack Zones, not individual Actors, with Ranged Actions.

entries.title: Objective and Epic Weapon Crate
entries.summary: Take or activate an Objective in the Survivor's Zone, following the Mission text.
details: Unless a Mission says otherwise, taking an Objective grants 5 AP.
Taking an Epic Weapon Crate grants a random available Epic Weapon; the Survivor may reorganize their inventory for free.

entries.title: Noise
entries.summary: Noisy attacks and door-opening actions attract Zombies.
details: Place one Noise token in the Zone where the Action resolved.
One Action produces at most one Noise token, regardless of dice or hits.
Noise tokens stay in their Zone and are removed during the End Phase.
Each Survivor miniature also counts as one Noise token.

entries.title: Zombie types
entries.summary: Walkers, Brutes, Runners and Abominations have different durability and activation rules.
details: Walkers and Runners are eliminated by a successful hit with Damage 1 or more.
Brutes require Damage 2; Damage 1 has no effect on them.
Abominations require Damage 3; a Molotov can eliminate them regardless of their Damage threshold.
A Runner normally receives 2 Actions when activated. Only one Abomination may be on the board at a time.

entries.title: Zombie attacks
entries.summary: A Zombie Attack automatically inflicts 1 Wound on a Survivor in the same Zone.
details: Players choose how to distribute the Wounds among Survivors in that Zone.
Resolve all attacks before Zombie movement.
Classic Survivors are usually eliminated after 3 Wounds; Kids after 2.

entries.title: Zombie movement and target selection
entries.summary: Zombies move toward the noisiest visible or audible target using a shortest route.
details: If Survivors are visible, Zombies target a Zone with visible Survivors that has the most Noise; otherwise they target the noisiest Zone.
Distance does not override a noisier target.
When equal shortest routes or equally noisy target Zones exist, Zombies may split by type; players decide uneven splits as described in the rules.

entries.title: Spawn cards, Rush and extra activations
entries.summary: Spawn cards use the highest Danger Level reached by any Survivor.
details: Resolve Spawn Zones in order, starting with the Starting Spawn Zone.
A Rush card's newly spawned Zombies immediately perform a free Activation.
An Extra Activation card spawns no Zombies in its designated Zone; instead, all Zombies of the indicated type on the board immediately activate, except at Blue Danger Level.
If the supply of a Zombie type runs out during spawning, place available miniatures, then all Zombies of that type immediately perform an extra Activation.

entries.title: Weapon characteristics
entries.summary: Weapon cards specify dice, Accuracy, Damage and Range.
details: Roll the weapon's listed number of dice for an attack.
Each die equal to or greater than the Accuracy value is a success; minimum Accuracy is always 2+.
Each successful hit inflicts the weapon's Damage on one target; extra hits are lost if all eligible targets are eliminated.
Dual identical weapons with the Dual symbol can be used together in one Action and must target the same Zone.

entries.title: Ranged targeting priority
entries.summary: Ranged hits are assigned by target priority, not chosen freely.
details: Priority order: Brute or Abomination (shooter chooses between them), then Walker, then Runner.
Resolve all targets at the current priority level before assigning hits to the next level.
Targeting Priority Order does not apply to Melee Actions.

entries.title: Friendly Fire
entries.summary: Missed Ranged attacks can hit Survivors in the targeted Zone.
details: A Survivor cannot hit themselves with their own attacks.
Each missed Ranged hit automatically hits a Survivor in the target Zone; players decide how to distribute those hits.
Melee misses never cause Friendly Fire.

entries.title: Special equipment traits
entries.summary: Some cards modify searching, combat or weapon availability.
details: A Flashlight grants Search: 2 cards; multiple Flashlights do not stack.
A Molotov eliminates all Actors in its target Zone, including Abominations, and is discarded after use.
Reloadable weapons must be reloaded after firing to be used again in the same Game Round; they reload freely during the End Phase.
Weapon Skills apply when making a Combat Action with that weapon; non-weapon Equipment Skills apply while the card is in the inventory.

entries.title: Cars
entries.summary: Car actions are available only when a Mission allows them.
details: Getting in or out and changing seats use Actions as described in the rules.
A Fast Drive moves through two consecutive Zones and performs a Car Attack in each entered Zone containing Zombies; a Slow Drive moves one Zone without attacking.
Cars cannot be driven into building Zones. Car Attacks can cause Friendly Fire to pedestrian Survivors in a Zone with Zombies.

entries.title: Dark Zones
entries.summary: Dark Zones make building exploration more dangerous when this optional mode is used.
details: Actors cannot trace Line of Sight to Dark Zones except at Range 0–1.
Ranged Attacks aimed at Dark Zones require Accuracy 6+ unless the Survivor has a Flashlight; applicable game effects still apply.
Melee Attacks are unaffected.

entries.title: Companions
entries.summary: Some Missions use Survivor miniatures as companions or support characters.
details: Mission-specific Companion rules take priority over the general rules.
A Companion stays with their Leader, has no inventory or Actions, and is eliminated upon receiving any Wound.
Unless the Mission says otherwise, eliminating a Companion causes the team to lose.

entries.title: Ultrared and difficulty tuning
entries.summary: Optional modes alter progression or the Zombie deck's difficulty.
details: In Ultrared Mode, a Survivor who reaches Red resets the Adrenaline tracker to 0, keeps their Skills and continues earning AP and additional Skills as described in the rules.
The rulebook groups Zombie cards #001–018 as easier, #019–036 as harder, and #037–040 as Extra Activations. These groups can be mixed to tune difficulty.

setupChecklist.title: Choose a Mission
setupChecklist.note: Use its specific setup instructions as the authority for board layout and components.

setupChecklist.title: Place the map tiles
setupChecklist.note: Match the Mission map and tile orientation.

setupChecklist.title: Place Spawn Zones, tokens and miniatures
setupChecklist.note: Follow the Mission and map markings. Objective and Epic Weapon Crate locations are predefined on tiles.

setupChecklist.title: Choose and distribute Survivors
setupChecklist.note: The standard game uses 6 Survivors, distributed among the players.

setupChecklist.title: Prepare each Survivor dashboard
setupChecklist.note: Assign the ID Card, colored base and 5 trackers to each Survivor.

setupChecklist.title: Prepare the card decks
setupChecklist.note: Separate and shuffle Starting Equipment (grey), Equipment (blue), Epic Weapons (red), Zombies (yellow) and Abominations.

setupChecklist.title: Deal Starting Equipment
setupChecklist.note: Deal randomly and as evenly as possible. Players decide who receives any extra card.

setupChecklist.title: Place Survivors in starting Zones
setupChecklist.note: Use the starting Zone(s) shown in the Mission.

setupChecklist.title: Set dashboard trackers
setupChecklist.note: Set Danger to 0, set the Wound tracker to the Survivor's starting Health, mark the Blue Skill, and place 3 trackers in reserve.

setupChecklist.title: Choose the First Player
setupChecklist.note: The player who received the Fire Axe as Starting Equipment takes the First Player token.
